t: C-Deterministic Autogenesis: Seeded World Simulator — Simple
name: C-Deterministic Autogenesis: Seeded World Simulator — Simple
title: C-Deterministic Autogenesis: Seeded World Simulator — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A simulator where the whole world grows from one seed: terrain, weather, and events all derive deterministically, so any moment can be replayed exactly. The seed is the world's DNA.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: World-space diversity across 1M seeds = 19.9 bits. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Seeded procedural simulation is standard in games and scientific modeling.
signature_version: Signature version: the autogenesis simulator — the chapter's 'deliberate creation of apparent chance' as a seeded world, with the 'full circle' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: derive everything from the seed, log the seed per run, and prove replayability.
math_note: World-space diversity across 1M seeds: 19.9 bits [verified]; Run log: 1000 h at 0.5 Mbps: 0.225 TB [verified]
safety: Reproducibility safety: any run that can't be replayed from its seed is a defect, not a feature.
how_it_works: The seed feeds layered generators; the simulator logs the seed with every run. The demo recomputes the diversity bits of the world space and the archive cost of the run log.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time
